spaces.name: Welcome
spaces.headline: Welcome to Awelen Entrepreneurs
spaces.desc:
I'm glad you're here. Awelen Entrepreneurs is a community for people who want to find, start and grow a business of their own, whether you're looking for your first idea or already leading a team.

You'll learn through short video courses, ask questions, book private coaching and meet other founders at live events. Please take two minutes to read how things work and the guidelines below. They keep this a safe and useful place for everyone.

rules.title: Be kind and respectful
rules.text: Treat every member the way you want to be treated. Disagree with ideas if you must, but never attack the person.

rules.title: No bullying or harassment
rules.text: Insults, mocking, threats, tribal, religious or gender slurs and unwanted private messages are not allowed. Such posts are removed, and anyone who repeats them is removed from the community.

rules.title: Ask questions freely
rules.text: No question is too small. Everyone here started somewhere, and your question often helps someone who was too shy to ask.

rules.title: Seek help early
rules.text: Stuck on a lesson, an idea or a payment? Post in Community, send Awele a message or book a coaching session. Don't struggle alone.

rules.title: Network to get more from your course
rules.text: Introduce yourself, comment on other people's posts and join a hangout. Founders who learn alongside others finish more courses and build stronger businesses.

rules.title: Share and celebrate
rules.text: Post your progress, what you learned and your wins, and cheer others on when they share theirs.

rules.title: No spam or hard selling
rules.text: No unrelated adverts, chain messages or get-rich-quick schemes. If you offer a service, apply to be listed as an affiliate expert instead.

rules.title: Respect privacy
rules.text: Don't share other members' phone numbers, messages or business details outside the community without their permission.

rules.title: Report concerns
rules.text: If something feels wrong, tell Awele through Contact. Reports are handled quietly and fairly.

modules.title: Module 1: Introduction to Business Model Development — The Founder's First Thinking

lessons.title: From idea to business
lessons.sum: The difference between an idea, a product and a business, and what a business model is in plain terms: how a business creates, delivers and captures value.

lessons.title: The founder's first thinking
lessons.sum: The questions every new owner should ask in the first 30 days: what problem, for whom, why me, why now, and what would success look like in a year.

lessons.title: Setting your early milestones
lessons.sum: Choosing the few markers that show real progress, such as the first 20 customer conversations, the business registered, the first prototype, the first paying customer and the first repeat customer.

lessons.title: Tasks and activities
lessons.sum: Breaking each milestone into weekly tasks, deciding who does what, and keeping a founder's journal of what was done and learned.

lessons.title: Capturing your assumptions
lessons.sum: Writing down every belief the plan rests on as a "We believe…" statement, for example "We believe busy parents will pay for weekly home delivery". Beliefs cover customers, what they will pay, what it will cost, who will help you and how fast you can grow. These statements are tested in Course 2.

lessons.title: From notes to a business model
lessons.sum: How milestones, tasks and assumptions couple together: each assumption lands on a block of the Business Model Canvas, each milestone becomes a test, and each task becomes a key activity. A first look at the nine blocks the rest of the course will walk through.

modules.title: Module 2: Vision, Mission, Values and Goals

lessons.title: Writing your vision
lessons.sum: Why purpose comes before the model, and how to describe the future you want to help create in one or two sentences people remember.

lessons.title: Writing your mission
lessons.sum: What you do, for whom and how, stated in a way your team can act on daily.

lessons.title: Core values and founder character
lessons.sum: Choosing the few values that will shape culture, hiring and how you treat customers and partners.

lessons.title: Mantra, tagline and motto
lessons.sum: Three short phrases that are often confused. This lesson explains each one, who it speaks to, and how to write your own.

lessons.title: Setting goals that mean something
lessons.sum: Turning vision into SMART goals and a small set of key results for the first 12 to 24 months.

lessons.title: Aligning purpose with the model
lessons.sum: A check that the business you are about to design actually serves the vision, mission and values you wrote.

lessons.title: Customers versus users versus payers
lessons.sum: Why the person who uses the product is not always the one who pays, and why both matter.

lessons.title: Segmenting your market
lessons.sum: Splitting the market by need, behaviour, location and ability to pay, and choosing which segment to serve first.

lessons.title: Building customer personas
lessons.sum: Turning research into a believable person with goals, frustrations and a typical day.

lessons.title: Jobs to be done
lessons.sum: Understanding the functional, emotional and social jobs a customer "hires" a product to do.

lessons.title: Pains and gains
lessons.sum: Mapping what annoys, blocks or worries the customer, and what would delight them.

lessons.title: Customer discovery interviews
lessons.sum: How to talk to real people without leading them, and how to record what you learn.

lessons.title: What a value proposition is (and is not)
lessons.sum: Moving from a list of features to the promise of value a customer actually feels.

lessons.title: Products and services
lessons.sum: Defining exactly what you offer, including the core product, support and extras.

lessons.title: Pain relievers and gain creators
lessons.sum: Linking each part of the offer to a specific pain or gain from Module 3.

lessons.title: Achieving fit
lessons.sum: Using the Value Proposition Canvas to check where the offer and the customer truly match.

lessons.title: Competitive positioning
lessons.sum: Studying alternatives, including doing nothing, and finding the space only you can own.

lessons.title: Writing the value proposition statement
lessons.sum: A one-sentence promise that customers understand in five seconds.

lessons.title: Choosing your business name
lessons.sum: What makes a strong name: easy to say, spell and remember, and true to the value proposition. Practical checks before you commit: company registry availability, domain name, social media handles and trademark search.

lessons.title: Designing your logo and visual identity
lessons.sum: The logo, colours and typefaces, and how to brief a designer. Bringing them together in a simple one-page brand guide.

lessons.title: Letterhead and business stationery
lessons.sum: Letterhead, business cards, email signature, and invoice, quotation and proposal templates that make a small business look established and trustworthy.

lessons.title: Your website and online presence
lessons.sum: What a first website must do, choosing a domain, building simply and affordably, and setting up social media and online business listings that match the brand.

lessons.title: Workspaces
lessons.sum: Choosing between a home office, shared or co-working space, a shop or office, and a fully virtual setup. How the space, signage and digital tools all express the brand to visitors and staff.

lessons.title: Messaging and communication
lessons.sum: Finding your brand voice, turning the value proposition and tagline into key messages, writing the elevator pitch, and keeping every channel consistent through a simple communication plan.

lessons.title: The customer journey
lessons.sum: Mapping the stages of awareness, consideration, purchase, delivery and after-sales.

lessons.title: Choosing your channels
lessons.sum: Direct versus partner channels, online versus physical, and what each costs.

lessons.title: Marketing and acquisition basics
lessons.sum: How customers first hear about you: referrals, social media, field sales, partnerships and events, all carrying the messages from Module 5.

lessons.title: Delivery and distribution
lessons.sum: Getting the product or service to the customer reliably, including logistics and last-mile realities.

lessons.title: Types of customer relationships
lessons.sum: Personal service, self-service, community and automated relationships, and when each fits.

lessons.title: Retention and loyalty
lessons.sum: Keeping customers coming back, and why keeping a customer is cheaper than finding a new one.

lessons.title: How businesses earn money
lessons.sum: The main revenue types: one-off sales, subscriptions, commissions, fees, licensing, advertising and rentals.

lessons.title: Choosing your revenue streams
lessons.sum: Matching how you charge to how the customer prefers to pay and how they get value.

lessons.title: Willingness to pay
lessons.sum: Simple ways to find out what customers will really pay before you set a price.

lessons.title: Pricing strategies
lessons.sum: Cost-plus, value-based, competitor-based, tiered and freemium pricing, with their strengths and traps.

lessons.title: Pricing in practice
lessons.sum: Discounts, bundles, payment terms and pricing for inflation and currency changes.

lessons.title: Revenue forecasting basics
lessons.sum: A simple, honest first forecast built from customer numbers and price, not hope.

lessons.title: What key activities are
lessons.sum: The handful of actions without which the value proposition cannot be delivered, linked back to the tasks listed in Module 1.

lessons.title: Types of key activities
lessons.sum: Production activities, problem-solving activities and platform or network activities, with examples of each.

lessons.title: Deriving activities from the model
lessons.sum: Working out what the value proposition, brand, channels and customer relationships require you to do every day.

lessons.title: Core versus supporting activities
lessons.sum: Separating what makes you different from what simply keeps the lights on, and deciding what to do in-house and what to outsource.

lessons.title: Processes and routines
lessons.sum: Turning key activities into simple, repeatable processes and standard operating procedures.

lessons.title: Measuring activity performance
lessons.sum: Setting a few key performance indicators and checking whether you have the capacity to deliver as you grow.

lessons.title: What key resources are
lessons.sum: The assets the business cannot work without, and why the wrong resource choices can sink a good idea.

lessons.title: Physical resources
lessons.sum: Premises, equipment, vehicles, inventory and technology infrastructure.

lessons.title: Human resources

lessons.title: Financial resources

lessons.title: Intellectual resources

lessons.title: Build, buy, rent or borrow

lessons.title: Why partners matter
lessons.sum: How partnerships save cost, reduce risk and open doors a new business cannot open alone.

lessons.title: Types of partnerships
lessons.sum: Suppliers, strategic alliances, joint ventures and partnerships with competitors.

lessons.title: What partners can do for you
lessons.sum: Gaining economies of scale, sharing risk and gaining access to activities or resources you lack, linked back to the gaps found in Modules 8 and 9.

lessons.title: Finding and assessing partners
lessons.sum: Where to look, what to check, and how to do basic due diligence before you commit.

lessons.title: Partnership agreements
lessons.sum: Agreeing roles, value sharing, performance standards, confidentiality and exit terms in writing.

lessons.title: Managing partner relationships
lessons.sum: Regular reviews, handling disagreements, and keeping partnerships healthy as both sides grow.

lessons.title: What a cost structure is
lessons.sum: Building the full cost picture from the activities, resources and partners in Modules 8 to 10.

lessons.title: Fixed and variable costs
lessons.sum: Costs that stay the same each month, such as rent and salaries, versus costs that rise with every sale, such as materials and delivery.

lessons.title: Direct costs and overheads
lessons.sum: Separating the cost of making and delivering the product from the cost of running the business.

lessons.title: Start-up costs versus running costs
lessons.sum: The one-off costs of getting started, such as equipment, registration and a first website, versus the monthly cost of staying open.

lessons.title: Cost-driven versus value-driven models
lessons.sum: Deciding whether to compete on low cost or on premium value, and how economies of scale and scope lower costs as you grow.

lessons.title: Cost budget, cash flow and runway
lessons.sum: Turning costs into a monthly budget and a 12-month cash flow, and why profitable businesses still fail when cash runs out.

lessons.title: What unit economics is, and choosing your unit
lessons.sum: Looking at the business one sale or one customer at a time. Examples of a "unit" from around the world: a cup of coffee, a ride, a monthly software subscription, a delivered order, a crate of fresh produce.

lessons.title: Contribution margin
lessons.sum: Price minus the variable cost of one unit, and what is left over to pay fixed costs and make a profit.

lessons.title: Break-even point
lessons.sum: Fixed costs divided by contribution margin: how many units you must sell each month before you stop losing money.

lessons.title: Customer acquisition cost (CAC)
lessons.sum: Total sales and marketing spend divided by the number of new customers won, and why it differs by channel.

lessons.title: Lifetime value (LTV) and payback
lessons.sum: The contribution a customer brings over their whole relationship with you, the LTV to CAC ratio (a common rule of thumb is at least 3 to 1), and how many months it takes to earn back the cost of winning a customer.

lessons.title: Improving your unit economics
lessons.sum: The four levers (raise the price, cut the variable cost, keep customers longer and win them more cheaply) and what to watch as you scale.

modules.title: Module 1: Desirability, Feasibility and Viability — Framing Your "We Believe…" Assumptions

lessons.title: The three lenses of a sound business
lessons.sum: A strong business sits where all three overlap: people want it (desirability), you can deliver it (feasibility), and it makes money and lasts (viability). Why a model that passes only one or two still fails.

lessons.title: Writing "We believe…" statements
lessons.sum: A simple template: "We believe that [this customer] will [do this] because [this reason]. We will know we are right when [this measurable signal] happens by [this date]." How to turn a vague hope into a statement that can be proven right or wrong.

lessons.title: Desirability: "We believe customers want…"
lessons.sum: Gathering the assumptions about customers, value proposition, brand and channels from Course 1, Modules 3 to 6.

lessons.title: Feasibility: "We believe we can deliver…"
lessons.sum: Gathering the assumptions about activities, resources and partners from Course 1, Modules 8 to 10.

lessons.title: Viability: "We believe we can earn…"
lessons.sum: Gathering the assumptions about revenue, pricing, costs and unit economics from Course 1, Modules 7, 11 and 12.

lessons.title: Ranking and scoring
lessons.sum: Placing each statement by how important it is and how little evidence you have, rating each lens red, amber or green, and choosing which statements to test first.

lessons.title: From "We believe…" to an experiment
lessons.sum: Choosing what to measure and setting a pass or fail line before the test starts.

lessons.title: Testing desirability
lessons.sum: Customer interviews, landing pages, pre-orders and "fake door" tests that show whether people will act, not just say yes.

lessons.title: Testing feasibility
lessons.sum: Pilot runs, supplier trials and doing the service by hand before building systems.

lessons.title: Testing viability
lessons.sum: Price tests, pilot sales, real cost quotes and checking the unit economics against actual results.

lessons.title: Reading the evidence honestly
lessons.sum: Separating real signals from polite feedback and wishful thinking.

lessons.title: Recording what you learn
lessons.sum: Marking each statement as confirmed, disproved or unclear, updating the scorecard, and keeping a simple learning log.

lessons.title: What prototyping means for a business
lessons.sum: Prototyping the product, the service experience and the business model itself.

lessons.title: Low-fidelity prototypes
lessons.sum: Sketches, paper models, storyboards and clickable mock-ups that cost little to make.

lessons.title: The minimum viable product
lessons.sum: Building the smallest version that delivers real value and tests the most important "We believe…" statements.

lessons.title: Prototyping the service
lessons.sum: Walking through the customer experience end to end and fixing the weak points.

lessons.title: Prototyping alternative models
lessons.sum: Sketching three or four different versions of your canvas to see which scores best on the three lenses.

lessons.title: Testing prototypes with customers
lessons.sum: Running user tests, gathering feedback and updating the scorecard.

lessons.title: Why good models still fail
lessons.sum: How changes in customers, technology, rules and the economy turn yesterday's confirmed beliefs into today's risks.

lessons.title: Scanning your environment
lessons.sum: Using simple tools such as PESTLE to watch the forces around the business.

lessons.title: Scenario planning
lessons.sum: Imagining best, worst and likely futures and rerunning the Desirability, Feasibility and Viability scorecard under each.

lessons.title: Building resilience into the model
lessons.sum: Diversifying revenue, suppliers, partners and channels so one shock does not sink the business.

lessons.title: Early warning signs
lessons.sum: The key numbers and signals that tell you a lens is turning amber or red and the model needs to change.

lessons.title: Leading through change
lessons.sum: Keeping the team, customers and partners with you when the model shifts.

lessons.title: The build, measure, learn loop
lessons.sum: How learning from each test feeds the next version of the model.

lessons.title: Persevere, adjust or pivot
lessons.sum: Clear signs for each choice, and how to decide without ego.

lessons.title: Types of pivots
lessons.sum: Customer, problem, channel, revenue and technology pivots, with examples from businesses around the world.

lessons.title: Versioning your canvas
lessons.sum: Keeping dated versions of the canvas, milestones and "We believe…" register so you can see how the model has grown.

lessons.title: From model to plan
lessons.sum: Turning a tested model into a business plan, budget and pitch.

lessons.title: Scaling the model
lessons.sum: What changes when you grow, and how to know you are ready to scale.

Now Run It is the bridge from Business Model Development to running the enterprise. Across 8 modules and 48 lessons you move from doing everything yourself to managing: setting the business up properly with the right legal structure and board, preparing the workplace, winning your first customers, bootstrapping on customer money, building the team and its rhythm, making decisions under uncertainty, and writing the business plan and pitch that raise money.

Zuri Kitchens, a Lagos cloud kitchen founded by Adaeze, runs through every module. Kofi, a top engineer in Accra newly promoted to lead six people, leads Modules 1, 6 and 7. Each lesson adds a short global or pan-African story.

courses.title: Deciding in the Fog: Head, Heart, Models and Tools for Leaders in Complexity
courses.headline: Decide well when the way ahead is not clear
courses.sub: For senior managers, C-suite executives and policymakers around the world.
courses.desc:
A seven-module, 56-lesson self-paced video course. It teaches leaders to decide well in complexity by bringing four things together: the Head (reasoning clearly, thinking from first principles and in probabilities, and guarding against bias), the Heart (values, emotion, intuition, conscience and courage), Models (frameworks for understanding the situation and the people in it, including Lewin, Kotter and ADKAR) and Tools (practical techniques for testing, weighing, committing and learning, including PCRM).

The Heart gets two full modules: one for the leader's inner life, and one for deciding on behalf of society. That second one is the Policymaker's Pause, the moment before a public decision when a leader must ask who carries its cost, when, and with what dignity.

Local and international cases run through every module. Two composite anchor cases, The Subsidy Reform and The Currency Redesign, come back again and again, each time through a different part of the course. They are told as design-and-impact studies with no blame or praise, and each ends with the questions any incoming government faces.

The course ends where most decision courses stop: choosing the right tool for the moment, making the call, carrying people with it, and building a culture where good decisions keep happening after you leave the room. Your capstone is a personal decision charter and a 90-day plan.

lessons.title: Dignity in design
lessons.sum: How policies make people feel, not only what they do. Told through Singapore's public housing, Brazil's Bolsa Família and Kenya's M-Pesa.

lessons.title: Right vs right
lessons.sum: Justice against mercy, truth against peace, individual against community, now against later. Told through Rwanda's Gacaca courts and South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission.

lessons.title: The next generation in the room
lessons.sum: Intergenerational decisions on resources, debt and climate. Botswana's diamond revenues and the Pula Fund, Norway's sovereign fund, and deciding for "seven generations".

lessons.title: Trust as public capital
lessons.sum: Legitimacy, consent and real listening, and what traditional councils teach modern institutions. Told through relief that arrived late or unevenly after the Subsidy Reform, and the trust it cost.

lessons.title: When decisions harm
lessons.sum: Acknowledging, repairing and restoring. Told through the Flint water crisis and Bhopal: what delay and denial cost.

lessons.title: Compassionate hard calls inside organisations
lessons.sum: Layoffs, closures, restructuring and hard people decisions done with dignity: fairness first, courage to act, empathy in execution. Pandemic-era layoffs handled well and badly, the alternatives to layoffs, and the toxic high performer.

modules.title: Module 5: Models — Making Sense of the Situation

lessons.title: Cynefin
lessons.sum: Matching how you decide to the kind of situation you are in: clear, complicated, complex or chaotic. Told through COVID-19 responses across countries.

lessons.title: The OODA loop
lessons.sum: Observe, orient, decide, act, for fast-moving situations. Told through a retailer facing same-day delivery, and security operations.

lessons.title: Recognition-primed decisions
lessons.sum: How experienced people decide in seconds. Lessons from firefighters and emergency physicians.

lessons.title: Who should decide?
lessons.sum: Decision rights (RAPID and DACI) and when to involve others (Vroom-Yetton). Who set the Currency Redesign deadline, and who had to carry it out: the executive, the central bank, the banks and the courts.

lessons.title: Expected value and regret minimization
lessons.sum: Weighing outcomes by likelihood, and asking which choice you will regret least, in investment and career decisions.

lessons.title: Real options thinking
lessons.sum: Keeping doors open in volatile environments. Told through phased market entry across African markets.

lessons.title: Lewin: is the system ready to move?
lessons.sum: Unfreeze, change and refreeze lightly, since stability rarely lasts long in complex settings. Was the economy "unfrozen" for the Subsidy Reform? Broad elite consensus, but little public preparation.

lessons.title: Kotter: moving organisations and nations
lessons.sum: Urgency, a guiding coalition, vision, early wins and anchoring in culture. Told through Rwanda's Vision 2020 and Estonia's digital government.

lessons.title: ADKAR: why good decisions die at adoption
lessons.sum: Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability and Reinforcement. Desire is an emotional stage that links back to the Heart. The slow uptake of central bank digital currencies set beside M-Pesa's rapid spread.

modules.title: Module 6: Tools — Practical Techniques for Better Calls

lessons.title: The pre-mortem
lessons.sum: Imagining the failure before it happens, clustering causes and planning countermeasures. A pre-mortem exercise on the Currency Redesign as if it were announcement week, and a bank's failed digital transformation.

lessons.title: Red teams and the formal devil's advocate
lessons.sum: Building challenge into the process. Told through the Cuban Missile Crisis deliberations.

lessons.title: Scenario planning
lessons.sum: Preparing for several futures instead of betting on one. Shell's 1970s scenarios before the oil shocks, and oil-price and currency scenarios for a post-subsidy economy.

lessons.title: PCRM: Pros, Cons, Risks, Mitigations
lessons.sum: Moving from "risky or not" to "risky but manageable", filling the four columns with finance, operations, HR and others in the room. A start-up weighing a buyout offer, and a retailer launching an e-commerce arm.

lessons.title: Weighted decision matrices
lessons.sum: Making trade-offs honest and visible, and pairing the matrix with PCRM, when choosing between competing investment options.

lessons.title: Safe-to-fail probes
lessons.sum: Small experiments before big commitments. Told through M-Pesa's pilot before scale, and regional relief pilots.

lessons.title: The decision journal
lessons.sum: Recording what you knew and expected at the time, so you build judgement over the years. A personal practice to keep.

lessons.title: The impact scan
lessons.sum: Mapping who benefits, who is harmed and who holds influence and interest, putting Module 4 into practice. An impact-scan exercise on the Subsidy Reform: urban commuters, rural farmers, transporters, the state and future generations.

modules.title: Module 7: Bringing It Together — Deciding With Others, Under Fire

lessons.title: Group decisions
lessons.sum: Consensus, consent and "disagree and commit" in boards and cabinets.

lessons.title: Making dissent safe
lessons.sum: Getting the truth into the room. The Bay of Pigs and the Cuban Missile Crisis: the same team, a very different process.

lessons.title: Crisis decisions
lessons.sum: Deciding when there is no time and the stakes are high, with five principles: stay grounded, people first, run the OODA loop, communicate before you have every answer, and balance speed with reflection. Told through Nigeria's 2014 Ebola response, Apollo 13 and Toyota's 2010 recall.

lessons.title: Communicating a decision
lessons.sum: The why, the trade-offs and what would change your mind. How the Subsidy Reform and the Currency Redesign were announced, and what a citizen needed to hear.

lessons.title: After-action reviews
lessons.sum: Learning without blame, drawn from the military after-action review.

lessons.title: Choosing the right tool for the moment
lessons.sum: Bringing it all together: what kind of situation is this, what kind of decision, which model and tool, then the Head and Heart checks. Told through Starbucks' 2018 store-closure day for training, and a telecom company facing digital competitors.

lessons.title: Building a decision culture
lessons.sum: Guardrails for local and central decisions, empowerment, transparency, psychological safety, debriefs, and rewarding good process even when results fail. Microsoft's culture shift from 2014, and a retail chain that let store managers decide.

lessons.title: Capstone: your decision charter and 90-day plan
lessons.sum: Write your personal charter across Head, Heart, Models and Tools, a 90-day roadmap for self, team and organisation, and a policy brief on one anchor case for an incoming government. Then the legacy close.

courses.title: Building Sustainable Wealth: From Breakthrough to Legacy
courses.headline: Your breakthrough is the spark. Your systems are the fire.
courses.sub: For founders, executives and professionals who want income to become wealth that lasts for generations.
courses.desc:
Earning well and building wealth are not the same thing. A big contract, a bonus or a business sale can fade within a few years, while steady, disciplined choices build wealth that outlives you. Across seven modules you measure what you really own, set money rules that hold, turn income into assets, put the right structures and advisers in place, protect what you build, use it to lift the people around you, and pass on capability as well as money.

The course teaches principles. It is not personal financial, legal or tax advice, and rules differ from country to country.

lessons.title: Inflation and currency risk

lessons.title: Income stops, assets keep working
lessons.sum: The salary versus the salary machine, and why the shift is first a change of mindset.

lessons.title: The asset map

lessons.title: Your business as your biggest asset

lessons.sum: What works, and the traps: illiquidity, land titles, over-concentration and the cost of upkeep.

lessons.title: When your wealth is just your job
lessons.sum: The 12-month test: what would still grow if you stepped away for a year. Built to Scale covers the business systems; this lesson looks at your wealth.

lessons.title: Ownership structures in plain language
lessons.sum: Personal names, companies, holding companies and trusts: what each one protects and what it costs.

lessons.title: Your investment policy
lessons.sum: Written rules for how family money is invested, so decisions are not made on emotion or tips.

lessons.title: Building your advisory team
lessons.sum: Accountant, lawyer, wealth manager and insurer: what each should do, and how to judge their advice.

lessons.title: Reporting on your own wealth
lessons.sum: A family balance sheet and a quarterly review, run like a well-governed company.

lessons.title: Workshop: your wealth structure map
lessons.sum: Draw who owns what, who decides, and who advises.

lessons.title: What you keep matters more than what you make
lessons.sum: The three causes of wealth loss, and the windfall that was gone within five years.

lessons.title: Diversification
lessons.sum: Not one company, one currency, one country or one type of asset.

lessons.title: Spending from your wealth safely
lessons.sum: Withdrawal rates in plain language, why the well-known 4% rule may not fit your economy, and how to set your own.

lessons.title: Insurance and risk protection
lessons.sum: Life, health, property and key-person cover, and which risks are worth insuring.

lessons.title: Wills, trusts and the documents that matter
lessons.sum: Getting your estate in order so your family is protected, not left in court.

lessons.title: Workshop: your wealth preservation plan
lessons.sum: Set your spending rule, your diversification targets and the documents to complete.

lessons.title: Shared prosperity is strategy
lessons.sum: Why thriving communities make thriving markets, and why wealth built on others' suffering is fragile.

lessons.title: The responsibility spectrum
lessons.sum: From extraction to compliance, engagement, integration and transformation.

lessons.title: Investing in your people and suppliers
lessons.sum: Fair pay, development and partnership as investments with returns you can measure.

lessons.title: Giving with a plan
lessons.sum: Personal giving, foundations and community projects run as well as a business.

lessons.title: Impact investing and patient capital
lessons.sum: Putting money to work for a financial return and a social good at the same time.

lessons.title: Workshop: your stakeholder map and impact plan
lessons.sum: Choose three initiatives that strengthen your business and the people around it.

modules.title: Module 7: Legacy — Wealth That Outlives You

lessons.title: Why family wealth fades
lessons.sum: The third-generation problem, and what the families who last do differently.

lessons.title: Passing on capability, not just money
lessons.sum: Teaching the next generation to earn, manage and grow wealth, at every age.

lessons.title: The family constitution
lessons.sum: Written values, rules and a family council for decisions about shared wealth.

lessons.title: Succession for the business and the wealth
lessons.sum: Choosing and preparing the next leader, and testing the handover before you need it.

lessons.sum: Treating heirs fairly, blended families, and keeping disputes out of court.

lessons.title: Capstone: your Sustainable Wealth Plan
lessons.sum: Bring every worksheet together into one plan, and write a letter to the next generation.

rules.title: Be kind and respectful
rules.text: Treat every member the way you want to be treated. Disagree with ideas if you must, but never attack the person.

rules.title: No bullying or harassment
rules.text: Insults, mocking, threats, tribal, religious or gender slurs and unwanted private messages are not allowed. Such posts are removed, and anyone who repeats them is removed from the community.

rules.title: Ask questions freely
rules.text: No question is too small. Everyone here started somewhere, and your question often helps someone who was too shy to ask.

rules.title: Seek help early
rules.text: Stuck on a lesson, an idea or a payment? Post in Community, send Awele a message or book a coaching session. Don't struggle alone.

rules.title: Network to get more from your course
rules.text: Introduce yourself, comment on other people's posts and join a hangout. Founders who learn alongside others finish more courses and build stronger businesses.

rules.title: Share and celebrate
rules.text: Post your progress, what you learned and your wins, and cheer others on when they share theirs.

rules.title: No spam or hard selling
rules.text: No unrelated adverts, chain messages or get-rich-quick schemes. If you offer a service, apply to be listed as an affiliate expert instead.

rules.title: Respect privacy
rules.text: Don't share other members' phone numbers, messages or business details outside the community without their permission.

rules.title: Report concerns
rules.text: If something feels wrong, tell Awele through Contact. Reports are handled quietly and fairly.
